properties.decision: The Documentation subsystem, its docs component, the capability of explaining reflow2 to a newcomer, and the README/SETUP artifacts read as a disconnected community to `detect_defects`, and that reading is ACCEPTED rather than bridged. The cluster is correctly modelled: the project contains the subsystem, the subsystem contains the component, the component owns the capability, and the artifacts both REALIZE the capability and DOCUMENT the project, the installer and the service. Those DOCUMENTS edges are true and are kept on their own merit — the tool's own guidance is to record a file that way when something would be wrong if it drifted out of step with the design, which is exactly the property the user asserted when he said documentation is part of the deliverable. They simply do not attach the cluster, because the structural network is built from DEPENDENCY relations only (a direct DEPENDS_ON, or a CONSUMES/PROVIDES contract collapsed through its Interface), and documenting a thing is not depending on it. No further edge can fix this without being a lie: documentation genuinely does not participate in the operational dependency graph.
properties.name: Documentation is part of the product but has no operational coupling, so its island is accepted — and the detector should learn this
properties.rationale: Decided 2026-07-24, immediately after the user answered that documentation belongs to reflow2 rather than sitting outside it ("it'd be like if I designed a fighter jet using reflow2, but then didn't deliver any documentation on it to the user"). Three bridges were attempted before accepting: project containment, which is how every other subsystem attaches; then DOCUMENTS edges to the project, the installer and the service. The detector still fired, and reading structure.rs explains why — the design network admits a defined TRACEABILITY set (SATISFIES, ALLOCATED_TO, REALIZES, VERIFIES, GOVERNED_BY, PROVIDES/CONSUMES, DEPENDS_ON, INCLUDES) and DOCUMENTS is simply not in it, while CONTAINS is deliberately excluded. That selectivity is correct and should not be weakened to silence this. THE GENERAL PRINCIPLE, which is why this is worth recording rather than shrugging at: dec:operational-spof already established that only things which OPERATE can be single points of failure, because the suggested fix — add redundancy — is meaningless for intent. The identical argument applies one category over. Only things that operate can be meaningfully disconnected FROM the operational network; a documentation subsystem has no operational coupling by its nature, so flagging it is a false positive of the BL-84 family, and the fix belongs in the detector rather than in the design. RESOLVED 2026-07-25, and NOT by the fix this decision anticipated — recorded because a decision that goes on claiming to accept something that no longer happens is exactly the drift this project exists to catch. The island dissolved on its own when cap:session-memory turned out to belong to BOTH cmp:docs and cmp:temporal: the user's point that a session's context is itself documentation gave documentation a genuine, non-cosmetic tie to the rest of the design, through ALLOCATED_TO edges that are true rather than manufactured. So the detector was never wrong about the topology — the topology changed, because the design gained a real connection it had been missing. The PRINCIPLE above stands unaltered and still applies to any future documentation-only cluster; only the specific defect it dispositioned has gone. Worth keeping as evidence for the detector fix: an island can be legitimate AND later dissolve legitimately, so the exemption must not be written in a way that hides a genuine disconnection.
